blindSummary: The country's uniform national framework applies; no state-specific law or enforcement pattern was found for this unit itself. But it sits inside the analysis's dominant regional finding: a sub-national region of the country recorded 38 of the 80 national killings of trans people in 2025 - nearly half the country total - and a national trans-rights organisation's victim profile names that region specifically. Regional exposure factors apply even without unit-level incidents on record.
blindSourceSummaries: Encyclopedia overview of the country's LGBTQ rights: the national legal timeline — recognition of same-sex unions and marriage (high court 2011/top council 2013), adoption, discrimination protections, gender identity and expression (the March 2018 rulings allowing name/gender-marker change without surgery), conversion therapy, military service and blood donation, plus a section listing non-binary marker rules by federal unit. The framework is national; unit-level variation is not covered by this page.

An international LGBT-rights organisation's country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex relations legal throughout the country; legal gender recognition possible by self-determination; a 2019 high-court ruling prohibits discrimination and hate crimes on SOGI grounds; marriage equality since 2013 with active repeal efforts in the national legislature; the country continues to have one of the highest rates of violence against sexual and gender minorities, particularly trans people; 3,000+ openly LGBTQ candidates ran in the 2024 municipal elections; a 2025 top civil-court ruling allows nonbinary civil-registry amendments; executive pro-rights positions vs a conservative legislature generating a surge of anti-LGBTIQ proposals.

A domestic law-firm guide to LGBTQ+ legal rights for foreign residents (updated April 2026): protections were established by the judiciary rather than statute — same-sex marriage, spousal-visa equality, joint adoption, name and gender-marker change without surgery, and criminalisation of homophobia and transphobia as equivalent to racism; major cities are broadly welcoming with legal infrastructure accustomed to same-sex marriages and name changes; the guide states smaller cities and rural areas may present more social friction, though legal rights are identical nationwide.
